title: Direct-to-buffer integer/float JSON formatting
impact: Removes one short `memcpy` and one `buf_write` indirection per INTEGER or FLOAT cell inside `write_json_to_buf` by reserving max-cell capacity once and pointing `fast_i64_to_str` / `fast_double_to_json_num` straight at `b->data + b->len`. Bit-identical JSON; same digit formatters and snprintf fallback. Focused `select_bytes_int_heavy.dart` A/B (order-flipped pair): **10k × 8 small ints −7.2 % / −7.4 %, 10k × 20 big ints (~18 digits) −8.7 % / −9.4 %, 1k × 2 ints −9.5 % / −7.8 %**, with the mixed-row guard inside ±2 %. Focused `select_bytes_real_int_fastpath.dart` A/B inherits the win on integer-valued REAL: **10k × 8 integral reals −8.6 % / −8.8 %, 10k × 20 integral reals −7.5 % / −7.6 %**, fractional-REAL guard within ±1.5 %. Existing int-extremes (`LLONG_MIN`/`LLONG_MAX`) and real-integer-valued selectBytes tests pass unchanged; no public API change.
